analysis.title: Impartial analysis of Measure EE

text: CITY ATTORNEY IMPARTIAL ANALYSIS OF MEASURE EE

Measure EE asks the voters of the City of San Bruno whether they want to amend the City's business license tax structure and rates so that every business pays a revised tax based on gross receipts, with two exceptions, as described below.

The City of San Bruno, like many cities, requires businesses that operate in the City to pay an annual business license tax to support the City's infrastructure, programs, and services. The current business license tax structure provides a variety of tax rates based on various factors for various types of business. These factors include square feet of office space, square feet of rental property, number of residential rooms for rent, average number of employees, number of vehicles used, number of residential units constructed, tiered amounts of gross receipts, number of bowling alleys, and number of amusement devices, among others.

Measure EE, if approved by the voters, simplifies the current business license tax structure by establishing a tax of $75 for gross receipts of $75,000 or less for all businesses, and by establishing tax rates per $1 ,000 of gross receipts in excess of $75,000 depending on the business classification, as follows:
$1.00 for "General/Retail," which includes retail sales, restaurants, wholesale trade, manufacturing, public utilities and administrative headquarters.
$2.00 for "Professional and Advanced," which includes services requiring training through higher education, vocational institutions, certification, licensing, or specialized professional skill.
$1.50 for "Real Property and Rental Activities," which includes leasing and renting.
$1.50 for "Services," which includes services that generally require minimal to no formal training, certification, or professional licensing.
$2.00 for "Contractors," which includes contractors, subcontractors, or builders.

The revised business license tax structure proposed by Measure EE reduces taxes for some businesses and increases taxes for others. Measure EE does not change the business license tax for cardrooms, which is based on the number of authorized tables, and airport parking facilities, which is 8.0% of gross receipts.

Measure EE was placed on the ballot by the San Bruno City Council. The City estimated that Measure EE would raise approximately $4,000,000 per year for use in the City. Measure EE provides that the tax will be in effect until ended by the voters.
The business license tax is a general tax, which means the revenue can be used for all general governmental purposes. Article XIIIC of the California

Constitution, commonly known as Proposition 218, requires Measure EE to be approved by a majority of the voters voting on the Measure. A "yes" vote on Measure EE is a vote to amend the City's business license tax ordinance to revise the business license tax rates and structure. A "no" vote on Measure EE is a vote to not amend the City's business license ordinance and maintain the current business license tax rates and structure.
Is/ Trisha Ortiz, City Attorney for the City of San Bruno

text: San Bruno is facing an unprecedented fiscal challenge. State actions threaten more than $20 million every year in revenue that funds the essential services our community relies on. At the same time, our Business License Tax, unchanged since 1999, no longer reflects today's economy, treats every business exactly the same regardless of impact, and charges lower marginal rates as businesses earn more. This outdated, regressive structure leaves San Bruno far behind neighboring cities and unable to sustainably fund basic services.

This measure is not a tax on residents. It is a modernization and simplification of our Business License Tax so it is fair, equitable, and aligned with real-world business activity. It replaces the obsolete 1999 formula with clear, reasonable rates based on business type and gross receipts, ensuring that large enterprises contribute appropriately while protecting small businesses by preserving the low $75 base rate.

Importantly, this measure does not tax affordable housing providers, who are exempt under state law. It also ensures that homeowners renting out rooms or ADUs on their primary residential property will continue to pay no fee.

By updating the tax schedule, San Bruno will generate approximately $4 million annually— critical funding to maintain rapid 911 emergency response, fix potholes and city streets, keep library programs strong, continue investing in programs at our Senior Center, and preserve parks and open spaces. These are core services that our residents depend on.
This measure is accountable, transparent, and includes annual independent audits.
Vote YES to protect essential services and keep San Bruno strong. Vote YES on Measure

text: Argument against Measure -San-Bruno-busin

Stop this huge new tax hike! City of San Bruno councilmembers are letting their greed show. Either that, or they don't understand the reality: Businesses don 't pay taxes. What?! Businesses create jobs, and goods that we value, and services we need. But they have countless expenses and considerations, to accomplish all that. You ask: How can it be that businesses "don't pay taxes"? Taxes are just another cost of doing business, which owners must pass along, to stay in business. They pass costs along to. .. e Customers, through higher prices; Employees, through lower wages/salaries; or • Shareholders, through lower returns on investments (e.g., our 401 (k)s or IRAS!) Remember the gigantic tariffs on imported electronics? how our favorite gadgets' prices spiked? Gadget businesses necessarily passed the tariff expense along to us, through higher prices. That illustrates a ftndamental law of economics — like gravity. But it's not just economists who feel those effects in everyday activities, like shopping or filling up the tank. The cost of living here is already too high. Nothing seems affordable! Businesses create goods and services that people want. Businesses create jobs that people want. Their outputs are amazing — enhancing so many lives. Don't trust politicians who would penalize businesses — the engine of our extraordinary standard of living — in order to fund pet projects. If Measure passes, San Bruno business owners who fall behind because skyrocketing taxation pushes customers away, may hatch plans to relocate to cities that appreciate them more. Don't tax what you want more of. Want more goods and services available at lower prices? Want more jobs to be available, at higher wages/salaries? Then please: Vote NO. Let's not penalize job and product providers! They help us, immeasurably, every day. Now let's help them:
Vote NO!
Silicon Valley Taxpayer Association's volunteers advocate for taxpayers throughout San Mateo County. Visit SVTaxpayers.org. [Argument ends here]

text: Rebuttal to Argument in Favor of Measure EE (San Bruno business license tax)

Stop this huge new tax hike! Beware: Proponents' claims about making taxes "fair" and "equitable" completely ignore reality: Businesses don 't pay taxes. Businesses create jobs, goods, services that we need and value. To do so, they have countless expenses and considerations. Taxes are just one cost of doing business, which owners must pass along, if they are to stay in business. They pass costs along to... o Customers (higher prices); • Employees (lower wages); or • Shareholders (lower returns on investments — our 401 (k)s!) Even small businesses who might be granted a modest license tax reduction would be harmed. When their larger suppliers are taxed more, the small businesses' costs rise accordingly — thus, the prices they charge us! (Remember: Businesses don 't pay taxes.) Don't trust politicians who neglect essential, core services like 911 emergency response, potholes, and streets, then have the nerve to stoke envy and penalize businesses to cover for their lack of planning. It's incredible how well businesses' goods, services, and iObs enhance our lives. But the cost of living here is already too high. Gas, groceries, rent — nothing seems affordable! And if Measure EE passes, San Bruno business owners, suffering when burdensome taxation costs push customers away, may relocate to cities who won't penalize them. Don't tax what you want more of. Want more goods and services, priced lower, and jobs, at higher salaries? Vote NO. Let's not penalize our job and product providers! Vote NO!
Silicon Valley Taxpayers Association 's volunteers support taxpayers throughout Santa Clara County. Visit SVTaxpayers.org. Ed

text: The opposition argument misunderstands both how San Bruno's Business License Tax works today and what this measure actually does. This is not a "huge new tax hike." It is a long-overdue modernization of a tax structure written over a quarter century ago that no longer reflects today's economy, treats every business exactly the same regardless of impact, and charges lower marginal rates as businesses earn more. This outdated system leaves San Bruno far behind neighboring cities and unable to fund essential services.

This measure does not tax residents. It does not increase costs for homeowners renting rooms or ADUs. It does not tax affordable housing providers, who are exempt under state law. And it preserves the current low $75 base rate for small businesses.

The claim that businesses "don't pay taxes" ignores reality. Every city in San Mateo County has a Business License Tax or equivalent structure. San Bruno's is simply obsolete. Updating it ensures that large enterprises contribute fairly based on their gross receipts, while small businesses continue paying the lowest rate.

The opposition also suggests this measure will drive businesses away. But neighboring cities already use modern gross-receipts systems—many with higher rates—and continue to attract and retain employers. San Bruno cannot maintain rapid 911 response, fix streets, keep library and senior programs strong, or preserve parks and open space without stable revenue.
Vote YES on Measure EE to protect essential services and keep San Bruno strong.
